records.name: Mendoza
records.current_summary: The national dossier found no trans-related statute, enforcement series or incident pattern specific to Mendoza, though it lists Mendoza's urban centre among the great-city areas where trans presence is policed; as in every province, the contravención/faltas police codes — documented as the instrument behind most arrests of trans and travesti people — remain in force, so the "no signal" classification reflects missing documentation rather than demonstrated safety. The February 2025 national decrees curtailing the Gender Identity Law (minors' transition treatments; prison placement of trans detainees) apply here as nationwide, within a deteriorating national picture (a record 227 anti-LGBT hate crimes in 2025, up 62% year-on-year).

records.name: Ogun
records.current_summary: No state-specific trans-related source was found for this division in the current research pass: no local incident series and no documented enforcement divergence from the national frame. The national law applies here in full — the Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014 (up to 14 years, extends to tourists, bans LGBTQ+ organisations and public expression of identity) plus the inherited criminal provisions; national monitoring recorded 89 extortions, 118 harassment incidents and more than 20 unlawful detentions of LGBTQ+ people by law-enforcement officials in 2024 alone, with detentions for "looking gay" and release on payment of a bribe reported. This division sits outside the twelve northern states that carry a separate religious-law death-penalty regime for same-sex conduct. Dating-app "kito" extortion gangs are a nationwide app-user risk, and foreign government travel advice warns LGBT travellers of arrest, violence and blackmail.

sources.claim: BBC News report (9 August 2024): police investigate the killing of a 33-year-old trans TikToker and sex worker known as "Abuja Area Mama", whose beaten body was found on a highway in the federal capital; she had reported a stabbing in September 2023 and had said she feared for her life; police described the victim as "a man fully dressed in female clothing with no means of identification"; the police chief ordered a "thorough and discreet" investigation.

Report (August 2026) on the latest UK travel advice for this country: warns LGBT+ travellers of arrest, violence, attacks, blackmail and intimidation; up to 14 years for same-sex sexual activity; some northern states' religious law can prescribe the death penalty; the 2014 Act also punishes assisting, attending or promoting same-sex relationships and LGBTQ+ organisations; separately warns of short-notice curfews and vehicle-movement restrictions, mobile-network shutdowns with little notice, and political rallies and communal violence.
